shots.text: In this town, everyone is an actor.
My mailman does Shakespeare between houses.
My family? Three generations of working actors.
My wife Linda: eleven years of dish soap ads.
My daughter Tess: "Sad Kid in Flu Commercial."
Grandma Bev: forty years playing the corpse.
And me? I'd just landed my first lead.
Then he walked in.
Sorry, mate. Is this the audition?
Robert Pattinson. He took my part. Very politely.
The next morning, there were two of him.
By Friday, forty.
They took Linda's soap ad.
Sorry. Lovely suds, though.
They took Tess's flu ad. They coughed better.
They took Grandma's corpse. He just lay there, brooding.
Every Help Wanted sign changed overnight: "ROB WANTED."
At dinner, Grandma slammed down her fork.
I've died on that stage four thousand times. I am NOT dying like this.
So we did what actors do. We rehearsed.
We tailed the hoodies to a warehouse outside town.
Inside: a machine, cranking out Robs.
And the real one, hiding in the corner.
I did one job. Please make it stop.
Linda distracted the guards.
Tough on grease... gentle on hands.
Tess fainted. Real tears. Flawless.
Grandma played dead. Her best corpse yet.
And I finally got my big scene, with a big red button.
Boom. Nothing left but empty hoodies.
Well, one stayed. He opens the coffee shop at six.
In this town, everyone is an actor. And now we're all working again.
